newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Some seek protection as market up.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Some seek protection as market up.

text.p: Upside momentum and fresh evidence of benign inflation in the U.S. helped push stocks higher Friday and some investors were beginning to take out downside protection by buying index puts, traders said.

"We have a lot of call buyers but we are seeing some put buyers too as we go higher," said Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in S&P 100 index .OEX options at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
He called overall volume moderate but said order flows in out-of-the-money puts were heavy, probably from investor hedging or speculating.
By about 1115 CST/1715 GMT, the most active OEX option was the February 715 put, with turnover of 7,035 contracts. The option, down 5/8 at 1-5/8, had open interest of 7,158.
The OEX was ahead 5.95, or about 0.80 percent, at 775.61. It reached a session high of 776.88.
The broader S&P 500 index .SPX was up 5.65, or about 0.70 percent, at 789.82.
March S&P 500 futures were ahead 5.45 at 793.40 after hitting a session high 794.80.
Fair value for March S&Ps was pegged at 3.40 points to cash.
Traders said arbitrage buy programs would be triggered at a premium of 4.80 points and arbitrage sell programs at a premium of 1.80 points.
The market was supported by a rally in bonds. Traders said both markets benefited from the fourth quarter gross domestic product report showing solid economic growth with low inflationary pressure.
Jay Shartsis, director of options trading at R.F. Lafferty & Co in New York, said sentiment indicators are reaching high levels but the market's upside momentum is overcoming any obstacles.
"The sentiment situation has deteriorated," he said. "The overall put/call ratio is probably worse, more bearish, than last May at the top.
"But there's a little thing called momentum," he said. "If this market has taught anybody anything, it's that momentum rules."
Callahan added that the morning's strong opening was helped by momentum from Thursday afternoon when stocks pushed to session highs and most indices closed just off those highs.
March S&P 500 futures closed Thursday at 787.95, just shy of their 788.25 session peak.
After losing more than 200 points in the January 21-28 period, the Dow industrial average .DJI was in striking distance of its record closing high of 6,883.90, reached on January 21.
Among other busy OEX puts, the February 710 traded 5,420 contracts and the February 750 traded 3,915.

The most popular OEX call was the February 795, which had turnover of 4,155 contracts. With the market up, the option gained 1-1/2 to 5-3/4. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
